title: Races With Something for Every Distance
seo_title: SEA Races With Something for Every Distance
meta_description: From a 1.5km fun run to a 50km ultra on the same race day -- the Southeast Asia races built to bring a whole training group, whatever distance each person is ready for.
dek: Getting a training group -- or a family -- to race together usually means picking one distance everyone can manage. These races solve that differently: six or more distance options on the same day, same venue, same start-line energy.

sections.heading: Vietnam's Techcombank Races: Six Distances, One Weekend
paragraphs: Both the Techcombank Ho Chi Minh City International Marathon and the Techcombank Hanoi International Marathon offer six distance options apiece -- from a 1.5km fun run up through the full 42.195km marathon -- on the same race day. That range means a first-timer attempting their first 5K and a training partner chasing a marathon PR can genuinely race together rather than at two separate events.

The Standard Chartered Hanoi Marathon Heritage Race offers a nearly identical spread (2.1km through the full marathon), giving Hanoi specifically two separate events built around this same wide-distance philosophy.

sections.heading: PMC Kabayanihan Run: Five Distances Including a 50K
paragraphs: The PMC Kabayanihan Run, organized by the Philippine Marine Corps in Taguig, stands out for going further in one direction than most multi-distance races -- alongside the standard 5K/10K/half/full spread, it adds a 50km ultra option, genuinely extending the day's distance range beyond the marathon for runners looking for more.

This kind of spread -- accessible entry-level distances alongside a serious ultra option -- is relatively rare in the region's race calendar, and worth knowing about specifically for a runner training toward an ultra distance without wanting to travel to a dedicated trail-ultra event.

sections.heading: The National MILO Marathon: Five Distances, Repeated City to City
paragraphs: The National MILO Marathon runs the same five-distance format -- 1km through 21.1km -- across multiple Philippine city legs (Tagbilaran, Cebu, Cagayan de Oro, and others), which means this particular distance spread, including a genuinely short 1km option suitable for young kids, is available in several different cities across the racing calendar rather than just once a year in one place.
That 1km option specifically matters for families -- it's short enough for a child to complete comfortably while parents attempt the 10K or half marathon at the same event.

sections.heading: Why Distance Range Is Worth Choosing a Race For
paragraphs: A race with only one or two distance options forces a group to either all attempt the same distance or split into separate events entirely -- both real friction points for a training group, a family, or a couple with different fitness levels. A genuinely wide distance spread removes that friction without anyone needing to over- or under-reach for the day.

This is a different selection criterion from this site's other Podium picks -- scenic, historic, or well-organized races don't automatically offer this kind of range, and it's worth checking a race's specific distance list before assuming it accommodates a mixed-ability group.

faqs.question: Are there Southeast Asia races with more than four distance options?
faqs.answer: Yes -- the Techcombank Ho Chi Minh City International Marathon and Techcombank Hanoi International Marathon both offer six distances from 1.5km to the full marathon, and the PMC Kabayanihan Run in the Philippines offers five distances including a 50km ultra option beyond the standard marathon.

faqs.question: Is there a race with a distance short enough for young kids?
faqs.answer: Yes -- the National MILO Marathon includes a 1km option across its multiple Philippine city legs, short enough for a child to complete comfortably while parents attempt a longer distance at the same event.

faqs.question: Why choose a race based on its number of distance options?
faqs.answer: A race with only one or two distances forces a training group or family to either all attempt the same distance or split into separate events. A genuinely wide distance spread removes that friction, letting people of different fitness levels race together at the same venue on the same day.
